cues.text: Type Four hypersensitivity is delayed: it takes several days to develop.
Unlike the other types, it is not antibody mediated. It is a cell-mediated response.
So the mediator is the helper T cell.
CD4+ Th1 helper T cells recognise antigen in a complex with MHC class two, on antigen-presenting cells.
Examples include the Mantoux test and chronic transplant rejection.
So for Type Four, the answer is helper T cells, not an antibody.
